title: How Thawte Turned From Web Consulting to Certificates in a Garage
conflicts: Sale price checked: VeriSign's own 20 December 1999 release says stock with an aggregate market value of $575 million (share count fixed by pre-closing price); The Register 2024 and Wikipedia say $575 million, the Cape Argus R3.5 billion. No real disagreement; the release's wording is used and no claim is made about what Shuttleworth realised as the share price moved.
notes: Arc changed from the slate's 'founding-decision' to 'change-of-direction' (consulting, then a secure server, then certificates). 'Bootstrapped' is a reading of the sources (privately held, bought from Shuttleworth, no investor reported), not a documented statement. Shuttleworth's biography and VeriSign's release are cited from Internet Archive copies over http because web.archive.org refused https during checking. Grocott's Mail copies the Cape Argus profile and is not cited. A blocked 1999 Business Report piece and reports of household-staff bonuses are not used.
